var, let, and const.
var: Function-scoped, can be redeclared and updated. It is hoisted and initialized with undefined.
let: Block-scoped, can be updated but not redeclared in the same scope. It is hoisted but not initialized.
const: Block-scoped, cannot be updated or redeclared.

Hoisting
Hoisting is a  behavior where declarations are moved to the top of their scope during compilation, before the code executes. 

console.log(a); // undefined
var a = 10;

Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)
period between when a variable is declared and when it is initialized. During this time, you cannot access variables declared with let or const.
Example
console.log(a); // ❌ ReferenceError
let a = 10;

Primitive types vs Reference types

Primitive types = Store actual value
number, string, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint
let a = 10;
let b = a; // copy of value

Reference types = Store reference (address) to data
object, array, function
let a = { x: 1 };
let b = a; // same reference

BigInt. ES11
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER 9007199254740991
let a = 20n;
let b = 5n;
console.log(a + b); // 25n

Nullish coalescing (??)  ES11
returns the right-hand value only if the left-hand value is null or undefined.
let name = null;
console.log(name ?? "Guest"); // Guest

Tree Shaking (ES6) 
is a build optimization technique that removes unused (dead) code from the final JavaScript bundle.

Numeric separators
Alllow format number by underscore ( _ )
const creditCard = 1234_5678_9012_3456;
console.log(creditCard); // 1234567890123456

Asynchronous programming
a way to perform tasks without blocking the execution of other code.

Promise 
asynchronous operation eventual completion or failure

States of a Promise
Pending – Initial state, neither fulfilled nor rejected.
Fulfilled – Operation completed successfully.
Rejected – Operation failed.


Promise chaining 
a way to execute asynchronous operations one after another using .then(), .catch(), and .finally().

Promise.all        = any reject    / all resolve
Promise.allSettled = never reject  / all settle
Promise.race       = first settle (resolve or reject)
Promise.any        = all reject    / first resolve

Async/await.

async function =  returns Promise. 
await = pauses the execution of an async function until a Promise settles

AbortController
lets you cancel asynchronous operations, 
most commonly fetch() requests.

Event Loop
The Event Loop is the mechanism process that manages the execution of synchronous and asynchronous code in JavaScript by coordinating the Call Stack and task queues, allowing JavaScript to handle multiple operations without blocking the main thread.

LIFO (Last In, First Out) 

Eventloop = manager
Call stack = Executor
task queue = functions queue that are waiting to run after the call stack is empty

Rendering blocking
Render-blocking  refers to resources that prevent a web page from being displayed quickly 
1. defer (recommended)  = Downloads while HTML parses 
<script src="app.js" defer></script> 
2. async  = Downloads in parallel 
<script src="app.js" async></script>
3. Move scripts to bottom 
4. Code splitting / lazy loading (advanced) 
import('./module.js')

Complexicity
Time Complexity → How much time does the code take as input grows?
Space Complexity → How much extra memory does the code use as input grows?

No loop                 => O(1)
1 loop                  => O(n)
2 nested loops          => O(n²)
3 nested loops          => O(n³)
Divide by 2 each step   => O(log n)
Sort + anything linear  => O(n log n)
